items.heading: Catch 22
items.summary: Editorial explaining that the wider-page format has not cut the magazine below 44 pages as club activity grows, and arguing the club must review how it manages its affairs.
items.text:
Catch 22

The introduction of the wider page 'Belgravian' was made with the hope of reducing pages and hence printing costs. By some strange coincidence the change in format occurred at a time when our whole range of activities expanded and try as I might I cannot provide an interesting and factual account of your activities in less than 44 pages. There was a time when your Hon. Editor could look forward to some kind of respite in the winter but what with the increasing interest of members in indoor competition as well as the despatch of teams onto the Continent no longer can the winter season be regarded as our quiet period. So what ? Well there is no doubt that the whole scope of our Club's work has increased and what with the new all weather Track at Battersea as well the planned improvements at Belgrave Hall things are likely to get even more demanding than hitherto.

The time is not far away when we will have to review the way we manage our affairs. Anyone who has attended recent Committee meetings at which representatives of all Sections, Sub Committees , Working Parties and so on discuss and control the affairs of the Club will realise that decission making is becoming more and more drawn out as the numbers attending increase. Add to this the fact that as our membership increases so our turnover moves into the small business bracket and you will see that some thought should be given to these matters in the not too distant future. The problem is - who's got the time to sit back and produce a master plan for the future ? CATCH 22!!

items.heading: grapevine
items.summary: Club gossip column: the Dormans' marriage, Oliver Foote's relay form, John Bicourt's film career, ex-Surrey AC members Jimmy Green, Walter Batson and George Williams, athletes taking time off to train, Bill Downey's illness and a walking section award.
items.text:
grapevine

Belated congratulations to Richard and Sonia Dorman on their marriage last June. Richard, who now lives in Nottingham, has made a welcome return to racing and is already well on the way to regaining his top form.

Oliver Foote went into hospital at the beginning of March to have his wisdom teeth removed. Four weeks later he was our fastest long leg runner in the Haig-Belgrave relay and by a big margin! We wonder if this technique for shedding weight will catch on.

While on the subject of improving racing performances it has not gone unnoticed that John Bicourt has started shaving his legs! We can report that this new development has something to do with John's new career in films and TV. Intrigued? Watch this space!

Among ex-Surrey AC members receiving the last copy of the 'Belgravian' was P.W.(Jimmy) Green. No stranger to us for he competed in Belgrave colours during World War 2. Jimmy of course needs no introduction as the man who started Athletics Weekly' after the war. Jimmy is now in his 70's but still trains local athletes.

Walter Batson, competitor in the first Barking to Southend Police walk, another former Surrey AC man and now a member of Belgrave is back on the road again after illness.

George Williams, a wonderful stylist, former Belgrave walker and International was recently seen in Bournemouth and sent his regards to all his 60's compratriats; Messrs Middleton, Vickers, Hall, etc..,

To reach the very top in todays athletics requires not only talent but complete dedication. Both John Gladwin and Stuart Paton have shown their commitment by changing occupations to give themselves more time for training. Mark Sinclair has gone one step further and, following a house move to Dorking is taking a 6 month sabatical to concentrate on his running. We wish all our dedicated young men the very best of good fortune in their endeavours.

Another member reaching for the top but in a somewhat different context is Don Anderson. Don has taken 6 weeks leave from his teaching post to undertake a training holiday in Kenya - At an altitude of 12000 Ft. We knew Don was determined to make our Southern League team!

Many of our regulars at Belgrave Hall have been asking after Bill Downey. Sadly soon after last years 25 by 1 mile relay Bill contracted a hepatic condition and has only recently resumed training. We wish him a speedy recovery.

Following their widespread successes in this years County Champs our Walking Section was presented by the Surrey & South London Newspapers Group wit[illegible] the Victor City Outstanding Sports Achievement Award for February.

items.summary: Obituary of Mrs E. R. Savage, widow of past president Dick Savage, club helper and Vice President, former Selsonia AC member and past president of Surrey County Womens AAA.
items.text:
In Memorium

MRS E R SAVAGE

We were saddened late in November to learn from Win Shepherd that her mother had died recently in hospital. Mrs Savage was in her 80's and had not enjoyed good health over the last few years. Nevertheless her interest in the Club never flagged and on a number of occasions during the last few years we were able to welcome her to our meetings.
Married to Past President the late Dick Savage she was a great worker for the Club, travelling with and supporting our teams. She was one of a gallant band of ladies who, half a century ago, cut piles of sandwiches and brewed gallons of tea for Belgrave socials which followed Club Championships.
A supporter of womens athletics she was a member of Selsonia AC now disbanded and was a Past President of Surrey County Womens AAA. Until the formation of our Ladies Section we were a mens Club but that did not prevent us from honouring her by making her a Vice President for years of service to Belgrave. A number of old friends from Belgrave attended the funeral to say 'Goodbye' to a fine lady. Our sympathies are extended to our other lady Vice President -her daughter Win- and the family.

Gordon Doubleday.

items.heading: The Lupton Shuffle
items.summary: History feature on Tommy Green's 1932 Olympic 50km walk gold and James M.K. Lupton's newspaper letter dismissing race walking as a 'professional shuffle', later answered by Green, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson and Ray Hall on the London to Brighton course; the original letter is reproduced.
items.text:
The Lupton Shuffle

At the Los Angeles Olympic Games of 1932 Tommy Green of Great Britain and Belgrave Harriers won the gold medal in the 50km walk. In the closing stages of a hard-fought race he beat the Latvian J. Dalinsch in a time of 4hrs 50mins 10 secs, after being nearly a minute down in third place at the three-quarter distance.

Tommy was one of Britain's two gold medallists at that Games (Tommy Hampson was the other at 800metres) and he returned to a hero's welcome. The press hung on his every word.

Prior to the 1933 London-Brighton Walk Tommy let it be known that he was out to be the first man to break the 8 hours barrier on the Brighton Road, and the Press got hold of the story.

The publicity clearly upset James M.K. Lupton of London Athletic Club who could not resist writing to the Editor of the West London Observer with his views on race walking. He put himself out on a most precarious limb by describing such walking as "professional shuffles" and ridiculing the supposition that anyone could legitimately walk from London to Brighton in under eight hours.

Well, Tommy won the race for the fourth time but failed by just 79 seconds to fulfill his target and prove Mr. Lupton wrong. And no one who saw Tommy Green walk competitively would question his mode of action.

Two years later Mr. Lupton was made to eat his words by the impeccable stylist Harold Whitlock who clocked 7:53:50 and went on to repeat Tommy Green's achievement by taking the 50km Olympic Gold Medal the following year in Berlin - again one of only two gold medals for Britain.

In 1957 the course was lengthened by ¾ mile to 53 miles 129 yards and another Olympic Gold Medallist-to-be, Don "Little Mouse" Thompson, set the sensational record of 7:35:12.

If James M.K. Lupton was famous for anything, it was setting himself up to be shot down by three of this country's greatest walkers.

Not to be outdone (and to make this story start and end on a Belgrave note) Past-President Ray Hall got in his own shot at Mr. Lupton in 1962 when he set a Stock Exchange record over the "Thompson" course of 7:58:38.

C.S.

SPORTS CORRESPONDENCE

RACE WALKING, OR THE "PROFESSIONAL SHUFFLE."

To the Editor, "W.L.O."

Sir,—I notice in the Press that Mr. T. W. Green has expressed his determination to walk from the Clock Tower, Westminster, to Brighton Aquarium, a distance of 51 miles, 1607 yards, in eight hours in the Surrey Walking Club's race on September 9th.

It makes anyone that knows what really legitimate walking is roar with laughter to think that any human being could cover the London to Brighton distance in eight hours.

Fancy anyone walking a mile in six minutes, 22 seconds, the present so-called world's record, and eight miles, 438 yards, in the hour, both impossible feats.

This race walking has been going on for a great number of years. It is not walking, but what used to be known in the eighties as the "Professional Shuffle." I have seen most of the so-called champions for the last half century, and I can say that I have never seen any honest walking amongst them. It is not walking, but a mix up between a walk, a run, a trot and a shuffle.

It took A. F. H. Newton 5 hours, 53 minutes, 43 seconds on November 13th, 1924, to run the London to Brighton course, which at once makes any one walking the distance in eight hours an absurdity.

All the walking records standing on the books to-day are nothing but "Professional Shuffles," and were never accomplished by fair and legitimate walking.

It is a very great pity that the International Amateur Federation and the Amateur Athletic Association recognises this mode of progression as legitimate walking, but to those that know anything about walking, it is nothing but a burlesque.—Yours, etc.,

JAMES M. K. LUPTON.
London Athletic Club,

His rise has been quite exceptional and as can be seen from results is now one of the team. Also we have had an assortment of individuals in team results, which bodes well for this year.

items.heading: WITH THE LADIES
items.summary: Women's section report by Ladies Secretary Derek Jones on the winter's cross country and circuit training, newcomers, the senior squad, Julia McGrath's promise and Gail Porter's three championship wins, thanks to helpers, UK ranking places for Jackie Harman and Lydia Montoute, and hopes of promotion to Division 2.
items.text:
After the Euphoria of the summer season Cross Country Training got off to a very slow start, with only 4 runners turning up on occasions. However, events seem to have snowballed and whatever the weather, normally 12 girls (on one occasion 18) have turned up at Belgrave Hall on Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings for a run over Wimbledon Common. Some of them positively dislike Cross Country Training but have persisted and have found that the training is keeping them fit. Circuit Training at Heathbrook Centre, due mainly to a late start also began slowly but more girls are coming along for training. We have had a recruitment drive going with some of the local schools and a few useful links have been forged. Some of the schools seem to think that it is a good thing that their children are benefiting from our training. Of the newcomers to Belgrave real promise has been shown in competition and training by Jackie Stone, Anita Davison, Kim Marsh, Julie Godfrey, Trudy Attrell, Sarah Wotherspoon, Sarah King, Sian Davies, Tania Morrison and Andrea Coore. Determination in training too has been shown by Nikki Marsh, Lisa Davison, Rachael Parrott, Christina Gauge, Amanda Grant and Mo O'Connell (until she was injured). Steady progress has been shown by sprinter Jessica Palmer who is one of those who dislikes Cross Country Training but looks better for the training and also competition and probably surprised herself by finishing 7th in the Club Cross Country Championships. Suzanne Jordan and Tracey Johnson have been fairly regular in their training but more determination is required in both traing and competition.

Unfortunately, the Senior Squad had been conspicuous by its absence but will be strengthened by the addition of Rosemary Honeychurch and Linda Sparks (regulars at Wimbledon and Heathbrook) Jackie Barclay has been a regular at Heathbrook but since moving house has found the trip to Wimbledon a bit far. Just to prove what a good all round athlete she is Jackie ran in the Surrey Road Relay and was second in the Club Cross Country Championships. Wendy Dunsford has not minded making the long trip from Harrow to train and compete on a number of occasions.

Although not a member of Belgrave for reasons which will become clear, 11 year old Julia McGrath has shown really exceptional promise, coming 4th in the Wandsworth Cross Country Championships, 11th in London Inter-Schools Cross Country and 7th in the London Inter-Boroughs. Julia has competed for us but will be moving to Birmingham shortly and we wish her well.

Pride of place must go to Gail Porter. Gail is now a triple champion and has shown determination and dedication in training. Her three wins were in the Wandsworth Schools Cross Country Championships (1st in 1981 and 3rd in 1980), the London Inter-Schools Cross Country Championships (7th in 1982) and the Junior Club Cross Country Champion (1st in 1982). All the races were won from the front and in the Wandsworth Schools at Morden Park she smashed the course record and finished well over a minute in front of the second placer.

From the beginning of 1983, we have had good attendances at cross country meetings and what with a number of parents showing interest and being prepared to come along in cold weather as well as finding that they have enjoyed each others company, the Belgrave contingent has grown. For instance, at the Mitcham AC/Prestige Meeting at Morden Park at the end of January, the Belgrave party totalled over 40 (compared with 9 in 1982). Also, the junior field in our own Cross Country Championships was the largest we have ever had. Some of the girls who have joined us have been shy and reserved but just by training and competing have gained in confidence and have surprised themselves with their own ability.

We now look forward to the summer season with some excitement and believe that with the additions to the squad we had last year, we are quite capable of gaining promotion to Division 2.

Just saying "thank you" seems a bit inadequate, but my thanks go to Harry Porter for his efforts in Cross Country Training and also in Circuit Training. Harry leads the Cross Country Pack Runs and is always urging the girls to do better and most have responded. My thanks also to Frank Simmons who although not always enjoying the best of health has been to most Wednesday and Sunday sessions and whose advice has been invaluable.

We still need help, however. So instead of sitting at home watching T.V. Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings why not come along and give a hand?. We need people to help especially at home meetings.

Congratulations to 2 Belgrave girls for getting into the U.K. Ranking Lists:-

Jackie Harman - 23rd in the U.K. Senior 100m (6th in the Inters).
21st in the U.K. Senior 200m (4th in the Inters).

Lydia Montoute - 14th in the U.K. Junior 200m.

Congratulations to Gail Porter and Julia McGrath who represented London in the English Schools Cross Country Championships on 26th March .

Ladies Secretary Derek Jones

items.heading: NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION
items.summary: Explanation that competing in a British League match only rules an athlete out of the next Southern League meeting, not the rest of the season.
items.text:
NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION

It is sometimes believed that participation in any one of the British League matches will preclude selection from Southern League competition for the rest of the season. This is not the case. If an athlete does compete in a British League match he is only precluded from the next Southern League meeting. Therefore all team members who competed in last September's qualifying match will not be eligable for the first Southern League Match whereas all those who did not compete will be eligible. It is, however, possible for Southern League athletes to compete in a subsequent British League Match without penalty.

items.summary: Report of the AAA Indoor Championships at Cosford, where Stu Paton won the 1500m from Gary Staines (3rd), Colin Gaynor ran in the 60m and Phil Lovell set a club pole vault record of 4.50m.
items.text:
JANUARY 29th 1983 - COSFORD - AAA INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.

We were well represented at this year's AAA's Indoor Championships and the video recorders worked overtime as Stu Paton and his training partner/ 2nd claim Belgravian Gary Staines lined up against a good class field in the 1500m which contained 3 visiting Americans. Ian Archibald stretched the field through 800m in 2 minutes. Gary tried to follow and with 400m to go Stu looked to have settled for 3rd. Ever eager to outsprint Gary Stu put in a long surge with such effect that he passed Gary at 300m out and kept the momentum going to turn a 15m deficit on Archibald at the 200m out mark into victory by 2m. Gary held on well for 3rd and only just missed the European qualifying mark.

Colin Gaynor showed early season form by running 12th fastest in the 60m while new signing Phil Lovell set a club polevault record with 4.50m to clinch 8th spot .

Still in the middle of their preparations for the National CC Championships Stu Paton and Gary Staines were called on at short notice to participate in the much published mile UK indoor attempt by Buckner. items.heading: TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982
items.summary: Round-up of Belgravians' places in the 1982 Scottish, UK junior, UK senior and UK women's age-group track and field rankings.
items.text:
TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982

The Scottish Association of Track Statisticians were the first to publish top rankings for the 1982 season. Belgravians were well placed in many events reflecting our growing strength.

Stuart Paton ranked 3rd in the Senior 800m with 1.48.9 and 4th in the Senior 1500m with 3.42.86. He topped the Scottish Junior rankings in both the 800 and 1500.

Steve Smullen ranked 15th in the 800m with 1.53.89, 17th in the 1500m with 3.53.2 and 9th in the 1 mile with 4.10.5 (All these performances were achieved prior to the Surrey AC amalgamation on August 31st 1982).

Mark Lindsay-Bayley ranked 9th in the 110mH with 15.3, and 13th in the 400mH with 56.9. His 6.50m long jump was good enough for 13th place in the Scottish rankings.

In the UK junior mens rankings for 82 Stuart Paton's times ranked him 5th in the 800 and 1st in the 1500. John Gladwin's 48.9 ranked him 20th in the 400, his 1.46.46 putting him top of the 800 Junior rankings.

But the most impressive improvement was in the number of Belgravians featuring in the UK Senior mens top 50 Rankings.

In the field events new member Phil Lovell's 4.70 was good enough to put him 10th in the pole vault with Mark Shippen's 4.30 being good enough for 30th. Derrick Williams ranked 18th in the long jump with 7.40 and 32nd in the triple jump with his 14.76. David Dawson ranked 49th in the shot with 14.27 and Ken Onagaluchi was equal 20th in the discus with 48.64.

Our young ladies too are beginning to make an impression. Jackie Harman's 11.81 100m was good enough for 5th place in the UK Intermediate women's lists (in fact 3 of the faster times were 11.8 windy hand timings, so in our book Jackie was good enough for second). The fast Intermediate 200m was 23.97 and Jackie was not far behind with 24.14 for 4th place. Lydia Montout ranked 14th in the Junior 200m with 25.7.

items.heading: BELGRAVE FORM NEW COLTS AND BOYS LEAGUE.
items.summary: Explains how, after losing the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League, Belgrave (led by Derek Crookes) formed the new Thameside League for colts and boys at the Battersea track.
items.text:
BELGRAVE FORM NEW COLTS AND BOYS LEAGUE.

When the Surrey/Belgrave merger took place last year we had hoped to use the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League to provide plenty of competition for our growing band of colts and boys. Mysteriously the Ebbisham League management decided that the Surrey slot should be relinquished. Not to worry we thought,Belgrave had been waiting to join for several years and so the vacancy would come to us anyway. Not on your nelly! We were passed over and so what to do? Well, to cut a short story even shorter, Derek Crookes came up with the idea of forming a new League based on the new all-weather track at Battersea. A quick advert in A.W. and we had a good enough response to get things going. The new League is to be known as the Thameside League- at least for this year. There are even more ambitious plans ahead. Several Clubs have indicated their interest in participating next year particularly if we include girls as well. Now that has the makings of a really good idea. Such a combined competition would create greater team spirit and would eliminate the expense of running separate teams to different venues. The GLC has been approached to see if they will support such a League and their initial response has been very encouraging
We ask therefore that all colts and boys take full advantage of the chances offered by this new League and turn out in force for every match!
(Also refer to the Hon. Secs. Notices on P.5).

Those of you who have kept a close watch on the developments at Battersea Park will have seen the excellent start made by the contractors after Christmas aided by a spell of reasonably dry weather. Hopes were high that an early opening might be possible but fate was to take a hand during the latter stages first, as a dock strike at Tilbury held up the top surface and second, as we moved into the wettest April on record. items.heading: EARLY SEASON SUCCESSES
items.summary: Early 1983 outdoor club records: Phil Lovell's 4.75m pole vault, Paul Richley's 8.14.5 junior 3000m and Dick Addison's 49.9 youth 400m, plus Oliver Foote's p.b. and John Gladwin's 3.56 1500m.
items.text:
EARLY SEASON SUCCESSES

No sooner had Steve Williams completed his comprehensive analysis of the existing Belgrave age records than the first results of the new outdoor Track and Field season arrived and almost immediately the records started to tumble.- A really good omen for the important season ahead.
In the Senior ranks Phil Lovell pushed his p.b. and our Pole Vault record to 4.75m at a S.Counties,Loughborough Univ.,London Univ.,Civil Service match held at West London on Wed. 27th April.
Paul Richley, also at the same meeting, lopped an astonishing 14 sec.s off his 3000m record to reduce our Junior best down to 8.14.5. In the same race Oliver Foote ran a p.b. 8.28.8, only 3 days after winning the Surrey 10000m title.
The other early season record was Dick Addison's Youth 400m time of 49.9 set while winning the Surrey title. This eliminated John Gladwin's 50.5 but John was not idle having stretched to an easy 3.56 1500m in his first outing at West London Stadium.

items.heading: SURREY TRACK AND FIELD CHAMPS - PART 1
items.summary: Stop-press note of seven Belgrave wins at part one of the Surrey Track and Field Championships at Croydon Arena, led by Dick Addison's record youth 400m.
items.text:
SURREY TRACK AND FIELD CHAMPS - PART 1

As we close for the Printers we learn of 7 wins in the Surrey Track and Field Championships held at Croydon Arena on 23rd and 24th April. Heading a list of excellent performances was the fine win in the Youths 400m by Dick Addison who erased Dave Mote's 6 year old record with an outstanding 49.9. Individual wins were also recorded by; Peter Gilbey- 3000 S/C- 9.29.3, Olly Foote- 10000m- 31.29, --- Derek Williams who won his first Decathlon with 5386 pts; and Paul Richley who won the Junior 3000m in 8.41.0
Wins were also recorded by the following relay squads; BOYS 4 x 100m; and the JUNIOR 4 x 200m................Fuller details next time !

We look forward to further successes in the second Part of the Championships which are to be held on May 16th-21st.

items.heading: PAUL RICHLEY PEAKS
items.summary: Paul Richley's win in the national U.20 indoor 3000m at Cosford (dated as printed 'March 18th 2983'), his 3rd in the English Schools cross country and 11th in the Junior Inter-Counties, where Stuart Paton dropped out ill.
items.text:
PAUL RICHLEY PEAKS

MARCH 18th 2983 - COSFORD - NATIONAL U.20 INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.

Paul Richley followed Stu. Paton's example and ventured hopefully onto the boards for the National U.20's Champs. The result was an unlooked for win and p.b to boot!! What this young man will achieve this summer is a subject for pleasant conjecture; but one thing is certain our Junior 3000m and 5000m records are due for revision.

1. P.Richley 8.28.14; 2. A.Pettigrew (WSE) 8.29.75; 3. J.Grix (Dartford) 8.37.46

MARCH 26th 1983 - CHESTERFIELD - ENGLISH SCHOOLS C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

Only 1 week after winning the U.K. U.20 Indoor Champs. Paul Richley was back in action again this time over the country and demonstrating his considerable strength and powers of recovery to finish a close 3rd to winner Chris Carter who later was to gain 10th place in the Junior International at Gateshead. Alister Horton ran well to be the first London runner home in 77th place having qualified by coming second in the London Schools Champs.

Senior Boys. 1. C.Carter (Sussex) 26.04; 2. T.Leach (S.Yorks.) 26.09; 3. P.Richley (Surrey) 26.19.........77. A.Horton (London) 28.16;

And!!! Not to sit idly by Paul Richley travelled to Birkenhead with Stuart Paton for the Junior Inter-Counties and despite feeling under the weather came through in the second half of the race to finish a very creditable 11th. Stu, Unfortunately,did the reverse. Surrey's Men's Team Manager,our own Clive Shippen reports that Stu hung on to 5th until he was taken ill just 600 m from the finish and failed to cross the line.

items.heading: YOUNG ATHLETES
items.summary: Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' winter season 1982-83, with commentary and race-by-race results for the colts (including the Surrey League first division title), boys and youths, and photographs of four young runners by Bill Laws.
items.text:
YOUNG ATHLETES

This is the second season of the new management, mars bars and all and the following results show an improvement on overall and individual results far beyond our expectations. Before detailed analysis, I would like to thank all the young athletes for their efforts during the winter, running through often very tough conditions. I would like to thank Duncan, Reg, Ted, Rosemary and Claire for sharing the load, also the increasing band of parents for solving the transport logistics of ferrying indistinguishable boys and mud. I never thought I would attend a race where the support for the Bel-boys outnumbers even the 'host' clubs but it has happened regularly this winter. I am grateful for this and the friendly atmosphere that exits within which the boys have maintained often dramatic improvement while sustaining an obvious enjoyment of the sport.

Reports by Ian Horton.

COLTS

We know if we want to eventually boast strong teams in each age group we must build from the base and therefore perhaps my greatest satisfaction at the completion of this season is to record we have 25 members in the colts section, the majority of whom have been active throughout the winter often fielding 3 teams. We have enjoyed 'many firsts'. We have fielded the first micro colts team and ran the first Belgrave mini colts championship, won by Adrian Ross and Second Russel Isles, both of whom (at the age of 10) have already made significant impact in the U.13 races. Teddy Davies is already an experienced campaigner and two years their junior, even so the age competition must be awarded to Stewart Booth, who at 7 ran a seasoned race at Canvey Island.

The colts were the most prominent in striking firsts for the Bels, pride of place going to taking the Surrey League 1st division title, winning convincingly against distinguished clubs, including Herne Hill, Croydon, Ranelagh. The most satisfying aspect being that eight boys contributed to the scoring team, G. Allison, B. Leigh, J. Caines, D. Steward, G. Webb, D. Cunningham, A. Ross and P. Whiston.

The first division individual title was won by Ben Leigh. Gareth Allison won the club championships, gained a creditable 8th in the Surrey C.C. Championship and represented Surrey County to finish 41st in the Inter-Counties 'B' race.

From this base I am optimistic we can develop strong colts and boys teams next season.

BOYS

The boys results sandwiched between the colts and youths may seem less inspiring but in fact have produced some of the most consistent performances. Not least is that of Garry McGurren, who as a first year boy was second in the club championship, first in the points scheme and lead the boys team to the highest overall position (7th) in the Herne Hill league. With an individual 10th overall. Kevin McDonagh backed up well with a third in the club championships and 2nd in points schemes. Although dogged by injury James Biesty won the club championship behind 2nd claim John Booth. Simon Beaumont, after a long illness, returned to racing late in the season to achieve a creditable 8th in the Herne Hill league. While new recruit Michael Bromley, improving in each race, moved up an age group to close the youth team at Ranelagh and secured a bronze team medal for his pains.

YOUTHS

A cursory glance at the results in this section shows we started with a bang. The team of John Warren, Andy North, Mike Blackmore and Dave Paimer gained a fourth in the Herne Hill League, then a bronze at Collingwood followed by a second to Aldershot in the Surrey League. So we travelled to Bournemouth with growing confidence and again were rewarded with an excellent third team place. Then on November 13th performed superbly in the Sutton & Cheam 4 x 1 mile relays with times of 4.40, 4.57, 4.50, and 4.52 averaging 4.52 miling( The course record previously averaged 5.02). Even so the team finished fourth to Bracknell. At that time we were not to know the ringing prediction in the past BELGRAVIAN (April 1982 P.29) was soon to be realised when injuries prevented this team running again for thr rest of the season.

So it was left to John Warren to fly the banner often without support and it is therefore to his credit that he has put together a string of outstanding performances ( including the Club Championship and 1st in the Points League, 5th at Bournemouth, 2nd at Canvey, and 2nd in the Ranelagh Open).

It is not surprising therefore that first and second year boys gave their support to maintain the combined Youths/Boys Surrey League position.

Good luck to John in the next C.C. season Junior Section where a comparative effort undoubtedly will reap higher rewards. Congratulations also to David Palmer, performing well throughout his first season with the Club, gaining a second in the Club Championships and second in the points table.

items.heading: ROAD AND COUNTRY
items.summary: The road and country captain's review of the 1982/83 season, lamenting poor support in key races and the failure to close a senior team in the National, while praising the juniors' retained Surrey title and individual runners.
items.text:
ROAD AND COUNTRY

A quick summary of the 1982/83 season would probably read like a typical 'end of term' report- 'Has shown promise but could do better and currently lacks the determination to do really well' Yet once again I am to record that the lack of support in some of the key races has left us with a result that is not only disappointing and frustrating to those who have turned out and tried hard, but shows us in a position that that belies our true potential. This was climaxed by our performance (or rather lack of it) in the National where we failed to complete a senior team. The honours must undoubtedly go to our Juniors for bringing home what creditable results we did have, with a special mention for the marvellous way in which they retained the Surrey title. Again though one is left wondering what might have been achieved in the latter part of the season if they could all have been fit and together at the same time

As the results show, for individual honours,congratulations are due to Stu Paton & Paul Richley for a string of top class performances throughout the season. Other noteworthy points include:-
- The impact made by our older Juniors and the consistant runs from ; Oliver Foote, Peter Gilbey, Don Anderson & Derek Slann without whom things would have been much worse.
- Don Andersons 'run of the season' by starting some 6 minutes behind the S of Thames Senior field and still finishing in the 200's.
- David North, still recovering from illness , running himself to a stop in the Southern C.C.
- The consistant runs of Simon Williamson & Leo Lyons until injury struck Leo.
- The emerging talents of Adam Christie & Mike Nouch and not forgetting Mark Sinclair's first (of many we hope) Club Senior C.C. title.
- Vet. International John Thresher flying from Canada to make our 12 stage relay team. John's interest & enthusiasm is a tonic to all who meet him on these visits.

Finally my thanks to Bill Laws & Tom Carter for helping out with the transportation of our team on so many occasions

GORDON BISC[illegible]

items.heading: BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS.
items.summary: Light-hearted report by W.R.L. on the club's first Boxing Day fancy dress 3.2 mile handicap road race at Wimbledon, with the full 47-place result.
items.text:
BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS.

When the idea of a Boxing Day Fancy Dress Handicap Road Race was first mooted there was little idea of the response it would attract from members. It is still not clear whether it was an excess of Xmas spirit; the desire to dress up; or just a bad bunch of programmes on the tele, but whatever the reason over 60 of our senior and junior members turned up in the most varied collection of costumes. Sigmund Freud would have had a field-day explaining the individual choices . There is little doubt of the terrific effort put in by all concerned. Indeed so good were some of the efforts that the HON. Handicapper could not identify them and Mick Gleaves cousin was heard to ask afterwards why he had not run!!

The good people of Wimbledon could not believe it as 'Noddy' Biscoe set the slower entrants on their way. But soon they were joining in the fun and rushing indoors to get cameras to record the strange sights.

The times were almost incidental but nonetheless the competitive edge showed as 'Father Christmas'-Paul Richley discarded his sack and 'Fly Me' stewardess John Gladwin threw away his handbag as they hauled in the early starters at sub 5 minute mile pace. Pete Gilbey as 3rd fastest was thought to have pulled a flanker as he was clad only in a nappy and large safety pin.

Rubic Cube- Pete Staples got in some usefull resistance training but the Fancy Dress competition was taken apart by the Pritchard family with Simon 'JIMMY' gaining 1st prize, closely followed by big'FAIRY' Brian who again proved he is everyones favourite. Not to be outdone in suspenders and Black stockings(Yes I know this is a family mag. but you should have been there) was 'St. Trinian' - Maureen.

The morning was concluded at Belgrave Hall with a hot punch bowl providing a fitting end to a really amusing event. It is rumoured that costumes are already being planned for next year. Me? Well I'm planning something, but on the other hand I might just take my camera along instead. I could make a fortune!!!

W.R.L.

(W) = Walker

items.summary: David J. Mote's report on Belgrave's first appearance at the Hermes Club Oostende Wellington Medley Relays on 27 March 1983, finishing sixth of 50 teams, with a course diagram and the leg-by-leg team.
items.text:
BELGRAVE CROSSES INTO EUROPE

MARCH 27th 1983 - OSTENDE - WELLINGTON MEDLEY RELAYS.

HERMES CLUB OOSTENDE have been organising the Wellington Medley Relays for 27 years and for the last 3 years a team from Surrey AC has crossed the Channel to compete. Hearing of our merger (how news travels) a Belgrave team was invited to compete along with 15 International Clubs to make up a total field of 50 teams. The race comprises of 12 legs ranging from 300 to 1200m. Due to the large number of competitors (600 in our race alone) the venue is a racecourse on the outskirts of Ostende and the race is held in front of the main grandstand to provide good viewing for a maximum capacity crowd and for the TV audience which follows these races with avid interest.

The UK teams created much interest and apart from the Bels there were strong contingents from Blackheath and Aldershot.

Our race started at 4pm with John Barry contesting the first 800m leg and he brought us in contention in 8th place. Everyone excelled themselves and the excitement rose as John Gladwin moved us into 2nd place on the 6th leg. The remaining runners tried desperately to take us into the lead as the race hotted up. For the spectators it was unbearable as the lead changed hands and after some 20 minutes only 10 seconds seperated the first 8 teams. The final surge saw Blackheath take victory in 20.08.6 with Belgrave 6th in 20.15.4 just one place ahead of Aldershot.

It was great to see the team spirit as our top track speedmen lined with our middle distance specialists. We even had a small band of vocal supporters and thanks to the Couzens and Pritchards for their backing. And finally special thanks to Leo Coy and Bob Bridges who respectively managed the team and organised the travel arrangements.

This year was an integration year where the team got it's feet under the table. I believe with the potential we have we can go back next year and turn the table over. Why not come and join us??

David.J.Mote.

items.heading: APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY.
items.summary: Gordon Biscoe's report on the Belgrave Haig road relay at Wimbledon on 9 April 1983, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 23rd of 41, with stage times and team results.
items.text:
APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY.

Up to seven days before the race we had the makings of a good team, one that would surely get us back into the first 9 places & hence qualify for the National 12 Stage Relay again. However once again it proved to be wishful thinking and during the ensueing week no less than 6 team changes and multiple variations to the running order had to be made. Injuries and illness accounted for most of the drop outs but not all, as even a race of this standard does not seem to have the attraction it once did in the days when people would give their back teeth to be in the team! However credit must go to those who still ran although one degree under.

The race itself was blessed with fine weather and a record entry and with fine opening runs on long & short legs by Olly Foote and Mark Sinclair it looked as though we would still make it. However it was not to be and we gradually dropped down the field to finish 23rd out of 41 teams some 6 places lower than in 1982 but some 2½ minutes faster! I do not propose to analyse the team performance in great detail but the highlight of the race for us was seeing John Gladwin well and truly back in action on the 6th stage in recording 15m31s, the second fastest on that leg and equal fourth fastest of the day.

Finally I would like to record my thanks to all those who helped to literally get the show on the road, from Bill Couzens who let me bully him into organising all the course markers-- once again a loyal band without whom the race just could not continue. To Clive Shippen and his equally able team who hardly ever see the race but who this year excelled themselves with a truly magnificent result sheet. Hope to see you all again next year!!!

Gordon Biscoe.

items.summary: Note on Channel 4 televising the English Schools championships and John Gladwin's selection for Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation sponsorship.
items.text:
SPONSORSHIP

Channel 4 has signed a 3 year contract to televise the English Schools Athletics Championships. This July more than 40 minutes of the events from Plymouth will be televised which no doubt pleases sponsors - The National Dairy Council.

Closer to home John Gladwin appeared on television following the announcement that he had been selected for special sponsorship by a panel which included both Brenden Foster and Dave Moorcroft. Eleven young athletes have already been selected for assistance via the Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation and a key factor in the choice of athlete has been that of ' high standards of dedication and self-discipline'. Peugeot Talbot plan to spend £25,000 on sponsorship over the next 3 years.
